title: omxplorer: one row, its video, its telemetry, its paper
subtitle: Nothing joins until you link it: a key, a file, a clock and a source, confirmed by you

nodes.label: You, or an agent
nodes.tech: pick a row · ask in words
nodes.desc: A person taps a row or types a question; an agent calls the same buttons as MCP tools. Same rules for both.

nodes.label: Fleet sheet
nodes.desc: DROID's success and failure sets (CC-BY-4.0), one row per episode: lab, robot, task, outcome, clip, source.

nodes.label: Links
nodes.desc: fleet.episode = telemetry.episode, fleet.clip = episode.file, telemetry.t ~ episode.t, fleet.source = paper.file. Each one typed or dragged, then confirmed.
nodes.notes: JOIN LINKED uses only the links you made: no guessed joins.

nodes.label: Episode video
nodes.desc: The failed episode's clip, opened by its link alone and decoded off the UI thread.

nodes.label: Telemetry
nodes.desc: Every frame of every episode: joint velocities, gripper, position and rotation. 16,847,616 rows; one episode slices out in about 2 ms.

nodes.label: DROID paper
nodes.desc: Every row names the same paper as its source, so the key link marks its passage: 'All DROID data is recorded at 15Hz' (page 15).

nodes.label: One cursor
nodes.desc: The video beside four lanes of telemetry on the video's clock: F00118's gripper opens over the box's edge at 12.7 s and the shirt falls.

nodes.label: omxcore
nodes.desc: The engine under omxplorer, in the same process. It runs the question's SQL over the linked tables and picks the CPU or the GPU.

flows.name: Why did it drop?
flows.desc: A failure opens by links alone.

steps.note: Pick F00118, a failed AUTOLab episode, in the fleet sheet.
Its episode key goes through the links you confirmed.
The clip link opens its video.
The key and the clock slice its 244 telemetry rows.
Four lanes land on the video's clock.
The gripper pinches at 5.3 s, opens over the box's edge at 12.7 s: the shirt falls outside.
'Failures where the gripper closed, let go and closed again.'
JOIN LINKED: fleet joined to telemetry on the key you linked, over 16.8M rows.
2,997 episodes, in about 40 ms (37–42 ms in the check's runs).
The answer is a card on the sheet; tap a row to open it.
Every row's source names the DROID paper.
The source link opens it as a document card.
'Recorded at 15Hz' is marked, read from the PDF's own text: provenance for every row.
